part.name: Combination open-jaw and ring wrench
part.description: A single-piece, constant-thickness wrench-like tool with a large open jaw at one end, a circular ring interface at the opposite end, and a long rectangular handle containing a shallow rounded-corner recess on its upper face. The STEP model is one solid with 26 faces, comprising 12 planar and 14 cylindrical faces.
part.symmetry_note: The part is approximately bilaterally symmetric about its longitudinal center plane and has a nominally uniform 15 mm thickness. The STEP data shows small left-right differences in the fitted outer cylindrical profiles and handle offsets, so symmetry is approximate rather than exact.

Section.name: Open jaw head
Section.function intent: Engages a nut, bolt head, or other two-flat component from the side so the tool can apply torque without requiring axial access over the fastener.
Section.physical behavior: The two inner flats react opposite contact forces from the fastener. Torque is carried around the rounded slot root into the outer jaw arms and then into the handle. The generous outer curves and root radii spread bending stress and reduce stress concentration at the base of the opening.
Section.geometry: A broad, approximately circular open-end head split by a centered U-shaped slot. The slot has two longitudinal planar walls, a transverse planar root, and cylindrical root blends. Large cylindrical patches form the external left and right jaw contours.
Section.location: At the negative-Z end of the part, opposite the circular ring end; shown at the upper end in the top and bottom views.

Section.name: Handle and continuous body
features included: Rounded transitions to both end heads
Section.function intent: Provides hand leverage and structurally connects the open jaw to the ring end while carrying torque and bending loads between the user's grip and either working interface.
Section.physical behavior: The long rectangular web behaves primarily as a beam under bending and torsion. Its broad upper and lower faces resist bending, while the full-depth side walls carry shear. Cylindrical transition bands at both ends smooth changes in width and distribute stress into the larger heads.
Section.geometry: An elongated, nearly rectangular bar approximately 20 mm wide and 15 mm thick, bounded by two long planar side faces. Curved transition patches connect the bar to the wider open-jaw head and the circular ring end. The STEP model uses one continuous top planar face and one continuous bottom planar face across the handle and both heads.
Section.location: Central longitudinal portion between the open jaw head and circular ring end.

Section.name: Upper handle recess
Section.function intent: Provides a visually and tactilely defined grip area while removing a small amount of material and preserving a raised perimeter rim along the handle.
Section.physical behavior: The approximately 1 mm deep recess reduces local surface height and mass without penetrating the handle. The surrounding rim retains most of the handle's bending section, while the rounded cavity corners reduce local notch stresses and avoid sharp internal corners.
Section.geometry: A long, shallow, rounded-rectangle pocket in the upper handle face. Its planar floor lies at y=14, one millimetre below the main top face at y=15. Four planar walls and four radius-1 cylindrical corner patches bound the pocket.
Section.location: Centered on the upper face of the central handle, extending longitudinally between the two end-head transition zones.

Section.name: Ring end
Section.function intent: Provides a closed circular interface that can receive a cylindrical pin, act as a hanging or mounting eye, or surround a compatible fastener depending on the intended application.
Section.physical behavior: The inner cylindrical wall transfers radial bearing loads into the surrounding annulus. The enlarged external ring distributes those loads around the hole and into the handle through the two rounded neck transitions. As a closed loop, it constrains radial translation of an inserted mating member while permitting rotation about the hole axis when clearance exists.
Section.geometry: A thick annular end feature with a nominal 10 mm radius through-hole and an approximately 15 mm outer radius. The hole axis is aligned with the part thickness direction. The outer circumference blends into the narrower handle on both sides.
Section.location: At the positive-Z end of the part, opposite the open jaw; shown at the lower end in the top and bottom views.

major_faces.description: Full-thickness cylindrical wall of the radius-10 circular through-hole.
